text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English engineer JOHN BUSBY, who built the first main water supply in Sydney from Lachlan Swamps (which later became Centennial Park) to the Hyde Park Resevoir, was born in 1765.

Irish/Australian inventor ROBERT SAVAGE, who held patents for a reaping machine, a stone crusher, a gold ore washer, a sewing machine, cement and paint, a torpedo and an earth scoop, was born in 1818.
American merchant GEORGE TRAIN, who earned himself a reputation as an irrepressible character in the goldrush days of Melbourne, was born in 1829.
Australian actor-manager BLAND HOLT, well known for his stage spectaculars at the Theatre Royal in Melbourne and the Lyceum Theatre in Sydney, was born in 1851.
British broadcaster MALCOLM MUGGERIDGE was born in 1903.
American actor STEVE MCQUEEN was born on this day in 1930.

Australian drummer COLIN PETERSON was born in 1946. He joined the 'Bee Gees' in 1967 one month after they had been signed to a recording contract. Two years later both he and guitarist VINCE MELOUNEY left the group following 'internal disagreements'.
Australian one-day cricket star DEAN JONES was born in 1961.
** EVENTS **
1401 : In his sweep through Asia and the Mediterranean,
the Tatar ruler TIMUR-I-LENK (TAMERLANE) conquered Damascus.
1603 : English QUEEN ELIZABETH I died at the age of 70,
with the final words "All my possessions for a moment of time".
1877 : The boat race between Oxford and Cambridge
Universities in London ended in a dead heat for the first time.
1882 : HENRY WADSWORTH LONGFELLOW, U.S. poet and author
of "Song of Hiawatha", died.
1905 : French author JULES VERNE ("Around The World In 80
Days", "20 Thousand Leagues Under The Sea"), died at the age of 77.
1922 : Only 3 horses out of the 32 that raced the GRAND
NATIONAL at Aintree, finished the race.
1944 : General ORDE WINGATE was killed in a plane crash
in Burma. He had led his "Chindits", a band of British, Gurkha and Burmese guerrillas, in raids behind Japanese lines from 1943-44.
1953 : QUEEN MARY, widow of England's KING GEORGE V,
died.
1958 : Rock and roll star ELVIS PRESLEY joined the U.S.
army for two years.
1976: Field Marshall BERNARD LAW MONTGOMERY, 1st
Viscount Montgomery of Alamein, died. He defeated the Germans at El Alamein and helped turn the course of World War Two in Africa.
1977 : DON CHIPP resigned from the FRASER Liberal
Government, to form the Australian Democrats. He resigned from Parliament in 1986.
1985 : Australian radio legend "ANDREA" (DOROTHY JENNER),
died at the age of 95. She went to Hollywood in the 1920's and became Australia's first female war correspondent during World War Two. She spent most of the war interned by the Japanese in Hong Kong.
1988 : An Israeli court sentenced technician MORDECAI
VANUNU to 18 years in jail for revealing details of the country's nuclear program to London's SUNDAY TIMES newspaper.
1989 : Two little known scientists, STANLEY PONS from the
University of Utah and MARTIN FLEISCHMANN of the University of Southampton, claimed to have unlocked the secret of low-temperature nuclear fusion.
1989 : The United States Government resumed a 40 million
dollar aid program to the Contra rebels in Nicaragua.
1990 : Indian peacekeeping forces withdrew from Sri
Lanka.
1991 : MADONNA won an Oscar for her song "Sooner or
later" from the movie "Dick Tracy", in which she also starred.
1994 : Federal Health Minister and Labor power-broker
GRAHAM RICHARDSON announced his resignation.
1994 : The self-proclaimed Bosnian Serb republic refused
to join a Moslem-Croat federation until U.N. sanctions on Serbia were lifted.
1995 : Britain said it was halting all routine army
patrols in Belfast for the first time in 25 years.
1996 : Iraqis voted in the country's first parliamentary
elections since the 1991 Gulf War. Most of the candidates registered as independents.
